suggestions.title: Match Scribe catalog external captions to the interface sans-serif reference
suggestions.observation: The external card captions in the unobscured applied-filter catalog have heavy serif glyphs. The reopened original sc-browse reference shows interface sans-serif external captions. Serif lettering inside a cover image is excluded from this comparison.

frozen_basis.declaration: The root family is Noto Sans SC; the external caption declares 17px/500 and inherits that family with single-line ellipsis.

suggestions.interpretation_note: HANDOFF's general book-title serif rule is broader; this observation uses the matching original route screenshot and its specific inherited caption declaration. Root final triage and deduplication are requested.
suggestions.suggested_remediation: Render the external catalog caption with the route-specific interface sans-serif 17px/500 treatment while preserving actual cover pixels, title data and caption allocations.

limitations: Scope is this eight-case batch only; no full/clean round or historical closure is asserted.
Related-state references permit actual content-driven sheet origins/heights; no geometry, typography, clipping or false-success waiver is applied.
Captured replay/state is separated from static appearance. No physical, performance, timing, evdev or lease qualification is made.
Existing Root-approved warning/tag/picker/callout findings and pending Reset/waiting-dot observations retain their earlier classification; this batch does not alter them.
Language empty/single-row states are judged against the related manager contract, not fictional reference rows.
The new caption glyph observation is pending Root's unique-group triage; it does not assert font-file identity and does not change older reports.

existing_finding_links.observation: The spare final tag row still grows across the panel; this is additional evidence for the existing group, not a new group.

pending_raw_observation_links.observation: Reset's plain heavy/no-underline treatment remains raw; its captured reset behavior does not approve the typography change.
